The **Acrobatics** skill (Dexterity; Armor Check Penalty) in Pathfinder 1e has several uses and modifiers, as detailed in the following sources:

### 1. **Balancing on Narrow Surfaces**  
   - **Base DCs**:  
     - Surface Width | DC  
     - >3 ft. | 0  
     - 1–3 ft. | 5  
     - 7–11 in. | 10  
     - 2–6 in. | 15  
     - <2 in. | 20  
   - **Modifiers**: Obstructed, slippery, sloped, or unsteady surfaces add +2 to +10 to DCs (see below).  
   - **Movement**: You move at half speed while balancing; full speed requires +5 to DC.  
   - **Failure**: Falling or being knocked prone.  

   **Source**: [Acrobatics Page](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics) (Table: "Acrobatics DC’s to Cross Narrow Surfaces").

---

### 2. **Modifiers for Circumstances**  
   | Condition | DC Modifier |  
   | --- | --- |  
   | Lightly obstructed (gravel) | +2 |  
   | Severely obstructed (rubble) | +5 |  
   | Slightly slippery (wet) | +2 |  
   | Severely slippery (icy) | +5 |  
   | Slightly sloped (<45°) | +2 |  
   | Severely sloped (>45°) | +5 |  
   | Severely unsteady (earthquake) | +10 |  

   **Only the most severe modifier per category applies**.  

   **Source**: [Consolidated Skills Optional Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/consolidated-skills-optional-rules) (Table: "Acrobatics Circumstances").

---

### 3. **Moving Through Threatened Squares**  
   - **DC**: Opponent’s CMD (to move through a threatened area) or 5 + CMD (to move through an enemy’s space).  
   - **Speed**: Half speed; full speed requires +10 to DC.  
   - **Failure**: Provokes an attack of opportunity.  

   **Source**: [Acrobatics Page](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics) (Table: "Acrobatics DC’s to Move Through Threatened Areas").

---

### 4. **Jumping and Falling**  
   - **Dive Damage**:  
     - Example: Diving from 50 ft. requires a DC 20 check; failure deals **2d3 nonlethal +1d6 damage**.  
   - **Falling**: A DC 15 check allows ignoring the first 10 feet of a fall.  
   - **High Jump**: Vertical reach depends on size (e.g., Medium = 8 ft. without jumping).  

   **Source**: [Acrobatics Page](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics) (Tables: "Dive Height" and "Vertical Reach").

---

### 5. **Advanced Ranks (Acrobatics Unchained)**  
   - **10 Ranks**: Use Acrobatics to avoid trip maneuvers or falling (DC 20 to reduce fall damage).  
   - **15 Ranks**: No attacks of opportunity when standing up from prone.  
   - **20 Ranks**: Double jump distance and never fall prone if conscious.  

   **Source**: [Acrobatics Page](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics) (Section: "Acrobatics Unchained").

---

The **Acrobatics** skill (Dexterity-based, with an Armor Check Penalty) in Pathfinder 1e is used for balance, movement, and avoiding attacks. Key details from the rules:

---

### **Core Uses**
1. **Balancing on Narrow Surfaces**  
   - **DCs depend on surface width** (see table). While balancing, you move at half speed unless you increase the DC by 5 for full speed. You’re flat-footed while balancing.  
   - **Example**: A 1–3 ft. wide surface has a base DC of 5.  
   - *Source*: [Acrobatics DC Table](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics#table-acrobatics-dcs-to-cross-narrow-surfaces)  

2. **Moving Through Threatened Squares**  
   - Use Acrobatics to avoid provoking attacks of opportunity. Move at half speed; full speed requires +10 to the DC.  
   - **DC**: Opponent’s CMD (for threatened areas) or 5 + CMD (for moving through an enemy’s space).  
   - *Source*: [Moving Through Threatened Areas](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics#table-acrobatics-dcs-to-move-through-threatened-areas)  

3. **Jumping and Falling**  
   - **Jumping**: Acrobatics determines jump distance. Faster base movement speeds (+4/rank above 30 ft.) and pole use (+2 bonus) modify checks.  
   - **Falling**: A DC 15 Acrobatics check ignores the first 10 feet of a deliberate fall.  
   - *Source*: [Jumping and Falling Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics#jumping-and-falling)  

---

### **Modifiers**
- **Surface Conditions** (stack with others, but only the most severe per category applies):  
  - Slippery (icy): +5 DC.  
  - Sloped (>45°): +5 DC.  
  - Earthquake (severely unsteady): +10 DC.  
  - *Source*: [Acrobatics Modifiers Table](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics#table-misc-acrobatics-modifiers)  

- **Loads/Armor**: Cannot use Acrobatics to move past foes while wearing medium/heavy armor or carrying medium/heavy loads (unless an ability allows full speed).  
  - *Source*: [Consolidated Skills Optional Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/consolidated-skills-optional-rules)  

---

### **Special Abilities at Higher Ranks**
- **10 Ranks**: Use Acrobatics to avoid trip maneuvers (–10 penalty) or replace Reflex saves to avoid falling.  
- **15 Ranks**: No attacks of opportunity when standing up from prone.  
- **20 Ranks**: Double Acrobatics check results for jumps and never fall prone from falls (if conscious).  
  - *Source*: [Acrobatics Unchained](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics#modifiers-acrobatics-unchained)  

---

### **Optional Rules (Consolidated Skills)**
- **Tumbling**: Move through threatened squares without provoking attacks (DC = opponent’s CMD). Full speed requires +10 to DC.  
- **Balance Checks**: Falling or being knocked prone if you fail a check. Recheck if damaged while balancing.  
  - *Source*: [Consolidated Skills Optional Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/consolidated-skills-optional-rules)  

---

The **Acrobatics** skill (Dexterity-based, with an Armor Check Penalty) in Pathfinder 1e is used for balance, movement, and avoiding attacks. Key details from the rules:

---

### **Core Uses**
1. **Balancing on Narrow Surfaces**  
   - **DCs depend on surface width** (see table). While balancing, you move at half speed unless you increase the DC by 5 for full speed. You’re flat-footed while balancing.  
   - **Example**: A 1–3 ft. wide surface has a base DC of 5.  
   - *Source*: [Acrobatics DC Table](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics#table-acrobatics-dcs-to-cross-narrow-surfaces)  

2. **Moving Through Threatened Squares**  
   - Use Acrobatics to avoid provoking attacks of opportunity. Move at half speed; full speed requires +10 to the DC.  
   - **DC**: Opponent’s CMD (for threatened areas) or 5 + CMD (for moving through an enemy’s space).  
   - *Source*: [Moving Through Threatened Areas](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics#table-acrobatics-dcs-to-move-through-threatened-areas)  

3. **Jumping and Falling**  
   - **Jumping**: Acrobatics determines jump distance. Faster base movement speeds (+4/rank above 30 ft.) and pole use (+2 bonus) modify checks.  
   - **Falling**: A DC 15 Acrobatics check ignores the first 10 feet of a deliberate fall.  
   - *Source*: [Jumping and Falling Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics#jumping-and-falling)  

---

### **Modifiers**
- **Surface Conditions** (stack with others, but only the most severe per category applies):  
  - Slippery (icy): +5 DC.  
  - Sloped (>45°): +5 DC.  
  - Earthquake (severely unsteady): +10 DC.  
  - *Source*: [Acrobatics Modifiers Table](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics#table-misc-acrobatics-modifiers)  

- **Loads/Armor**: Cannot use Acrobatics to move past foes while wearing medium/heavy armor or carrying medium/heavy loads (unless an ability allows full speed).  
  - *Source*: [Consolidated Skills Optional Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/consolidated-skills-optional-rules)  

---

### **Special Abilities at Higher Ranks**
- **10 Ranks**: Use Acrobatics to avoid trip maneuvers (–10 penalty) or replace Reflex saves to avoid falling.  
- **15 Ranks**: No attacks of opportunity when standing up from prone.  
- **20 Ranks**: Double Acrobatics check results for jumps and never fall prone from falls (if conscious).  
  - *Source*: [Acrobatics Unchained](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/acrobatics#modifiers-acrobatics-unchained)  

---

### **Optional Rules (Consolidated Skills)**
- **Tumbling**: Move through threatened squares without provoking attacks (DC = opponent’s CMD). Full speed requires +10 to DC.  
- **Balance Checks**: Falling or being knocked prone if you fail a check. Recheck if damaged while balancing.  
  - *Source*: [Consolidated Skills Optional Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/consolidated-skills-optional-rules)  

---

The **Stealth** skill (Dexterity; Armor Check Penalty) in Pathfinder 1e allows characters to avoid detection, enabling them to hide or move silently. Here are key details from the rules:

### **Core Mechanics**
- **Opposed Checks**: A Stealth check is opposed by a creature's Perception check. If the Stealth check succeeds, the creature is unaware of the user and treats them as having **total concealment**.
- **Movement**: You can move up to **half your normal speed** without penalty. Moving faster than half speed but less than full speed incurs a **–5 penalty**. Stealth is impossible while **attacking, running, or charging**.
- **Breaking Stealth**: If you start your turn using Stealth, you can leave cover/concealment and remain unnoticed if you succeed at a Stealth check and end your turn in cover/concealment. Stealth ends immediately after making an attack (except during **sniping**).

### **Modifiers**
- **Size**: Creatures gain bonuses/penalties based on size (e.g., *Fine* +16, *Medium* +0, *Colossal* –16).
- **Being Observed**: If observed (e.g., by sight), Stealth cannot be used unless the observer is distracted (e.g., by a **Bluff** check). Such checks incur a **–10 penalty**.
- **Magic**: Being **invisible** grants a **+40 bonus** (if immobile) or **+20** (if moving).
- **Feats**: The **Stealthy** feat provides a bonus on Stealth checks.

### **Special Cases**
- **Hiding Behind Creatures**: Cover provided by a creature **one size larger** allows Stealth at a **–10 penalty** (–20 if the creature is aware of you). Hiding under a creature **two sizes larger** also grants a –10 penalty (–20 if aware).
- **Sniping**: Using Stealth immediately after a ranged attack is a **move action**. At **20 ranks** in Stealth, the target is denied its Dexterity bonus against all your attacks until the start of your next turn.

### **Optional Rules (Stealth Unchained)**
- **Skill Unlocks** (attained at specific ranks):
  - **5 Ranks**: Reduce Stealth penalty from sniping by 10.
  - **10 Ranks**: Halve penalties for moving quickly (including sniping).
  - **15 Ranks**: Deny target's Dexterity bonus against your attacks **until the end of your turn**.
  - **20 Ranks**: Deny Dexterity bonus **until the start of your next turn**.

### **Environmental Effects**
- **Forests**: 
  - Detection distances vary by density (sparse: 3d6 × 10 ft, dense: 2d6 × 10 ft).
  - Undergrowth provides **concealment**, and background noise increases Perception DCs by **2 per 10 feet** (vs. 1 in open areas).

For full details, see: [https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/stealth](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/stealth).

The spell you're looking for is **Invisibility**. Here are the key details from the [official page](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/all-spells/i/invisibility):

- **School**: Illusion (Glamer)  
- **Level**: Various (e.g., 2nd-level for wizards, 4th-level for some classes)  
- **Range**: Personal or touch  
- **Target**: You or a creature/object weighing ≤100 lbs./level  
- **Duration**: 1 minute/level (D)  
- **Saving Throw**: Will negates (harmless)  
- **Spell Resistance**: Yes (harmless)  

### Effects:
- Makes the target invisible (including carried gear).  
- Ends if the subject **attacks any creature** (attacking includes spells targeting foes).  
- Invisible creatures gain a +40 bonus on Stealth checks while stationary, reduced to +20 when moving.  
- Items dropped by invisible creatures become visible, but light sources remain invisible.  

A variant, **Invisibility, Greater** (also on the page), does not end if the subject attacks. Another variant, **Invisibility, Mass**, affects multiple targets.  

For a shorter-duration option, **Vanish** (linked in the results) works like Invisibility but lasts only 1 round/level (max 5 rounds).

question: class feature that lets a rogue deal bonus damage from sneaking
answer:
The primary class feature that allows a rogue to deal bonus damage from sneaking is **Sneak Attack**, detailed in the [Rogue class](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/rogue) and [Unchained Rogue class](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/unchained-classes/rogue-unchained). 

### Key Details:
- **Extra Damage**: A rogue deals **1d6 precision damage** at 1st level, increasing by 1d6 every two levels. This damage applies when:
  - The target is denied a Dexterity bonus to AC (e.g., due to being flanked or otherwise incapacitated).
  - The rogue flanks the target.
- **Ranged Attacks**: Only count as sneak attacks if the target is within **30 feet**.
- **Nonlethal Damage**: With weapons like saps or whips, a rogue can deal nonlethal damage instead of lethal via sneak attack (but not with lethal weapons, even with penalties).

### Additional Talents (Advanced Options):
- **Sneaky Maneuver** (Ex): Allows a rogue to replace sneak attack damage with combat maneuvers (disarm, trip, etc.) with a –2 penalty on the initial attack.
- **Crippling Strike** (Ex): Adds **2 points of Strength damage** to a sneak attack.
- **Master Strike** (Ex, 20th level): Lets the rogue choose effects like sleep, paralysis, or slaying when dealing sneak attack damage.

The primary class feature that allows a rogue to deal bonus damage from sneaking is **Sneak Attack**, detailed in the [Rogue class](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/rogue) and [Unchained Rogue class](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/unchained-classes/rogue-unchained). 

### Key Details:
- **Extra Damage**: A rogue deals **1d6 precision damage** at 1st level, increasing by 1d6 every two levels. This damage applies when:
  - The target is denied a Dexterity bonus to AC (e.g., due to being flanked or otherwise incapacitated).
  - The rogue flanks the target.
- **Ranged Attacks**: Only count as sneak attacks if the target is within **30 feet**.
- **Nonlethal Damage**: With weapons like saps or whips, a rogue can deal nonlethal damage instead of lethal via sneak attack (but not with lethal weapons, even with penalties).

### Additional Talents (Advanced Options):
- **Sneaky Maneuver** (Ex): Allows a rogue to replace sneak attack damage with combat maneuvers (disarm, trip, etc.) with a –2 penalty on the initial attack.
- **Crippling Strike** (Ex): Adds **2 points of Strength damage** to a sneak attack.
- **Master Strike** (Ex, 20th level): Lets the rogue choose effects like sleep, paralysis, or slaying when dealing sneak attack damage.

For full rules, see the [Rogue class page](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/rogue) or [Unchained Rogue](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/unchained-classes/rogue-unchained).

question: spell that lets you talk to animals
answer:
The spell **Speak with Animals** allows you to communicate with animals. It lets you ask questions and receive answers, though animals remain at their normal attitudes toward you (friendly, indifferent, or hostile). Wary animals may be evasive, while simpler ones might give inane responses. If an animal is already friendly, it might perform favors. This spell is found at [https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/all-spells/s/speak-with-animals](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/all-spells/s/speak-with-animals).

A related spell, **Call Animal**, summons an animal of a specified type (CR ≤ caster level) to your location, but it does not grant communication abilities. The called animal starts with an indifferent attitude. This is detailed at [https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/all-spells/c/call-animal](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/all-spells/c/call-animal).

Additionally, the **Animal Friend** talent (from the *Spheres of Power* variant magic rules) lets you spend a spell point to make animals treat you as a friend for 1 minute per caster level, enabling communication. This is covered at [https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/variant-magic-rules/spheres-of-power/using-the-spheres](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/variant-magic-rules/spheres-of-power/using-the-spheres).

   - **Source**: [Remove Curse](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/all-spells/r/remove-curse).

Both spells are effective for removing curses, but **Break Enchantment** is broader in scope (e.g., transmutations), while **Remove Curse** is specifically designed for curses. Neither removes curses from *permanent magic items* outright.

The ability to instantly move to a distant location in Pathfinder 1e is primarily achieved through spells like **Teleport** and **Interplanetary Teleport**, as well as variant magic rules like **Dimensional Shift**. Here's a summary of key options:

1. **Teleport** (Wizard 5, etc.)  
   - **Range**: Up to 100 miles per caster level.  
   - **Details**: Transport yourself and others (with contact) to a known location. Requires a clear mental image of the destination. Interplanar travel is not possible.  
   - **Source**: [Teleport Spell](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/all-spells/t/teleport).

2. **Teleport, Greater** (Wizard 7, etc.)  
   - **Range**: No limit.  
   - **Details**: No chance of arriving off-target. Requires a reliable description of the destination (not necessarily seen before).  
   - **Source**: [Teleport Spell](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/all-spells/t/teleport).

3. **Interplanetary Teleport** (Wizard 9, etc.)  
   - **Range**: No limit (between planets).  
   - **Details**: Requires a specific grasp of the destination world (e.g., “third planet from the sun”). If no safe landing exists, the spell fails.  
   - **Source**: [Interplanetary Teleport](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/all-spells/i/interplanetary-teleport).

4. **Dimensional Shift** (Word of Power, Teleportation)  
   - **Range**: Same as the wordspell’s range.  
   - **Details**: Teleports targets to another plane of existence. The destination is within 5–500 miles of the intended location.  
   - **Source**: [Dimensional Shift](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic/variant-magic-rules/words-of-power/effect-words/dimensional-shift).

Each spell has trade-offs: **Teleport** is reliable for known locations, **Teleport, Greater** offers precision without prior sight, and **Interplanetary Teleport** allows planetary travel but requires specific knowledge. Variants like **Dimensional Shift** introduce planar travel but with less control.

question: feat that improves your chance of scoring a critical hit
answer:
The feats listed in the search results (e.g., **Crippling Critical**, **Exhausting Critical**, **Blinding Critical**, etc.) do not improve the chance of scoring a critical hit. Instead, they enhance the **effects** of a critical hit once it is confirmed. For example:

- **Crippling Critical** halves an opponent’s speed for 1 minute (or less on a save).
- **Exhausting Critical** immediately exhausts a target.
- **Blinding Critical** blinds a target (or dazzles it on a save).

These feats require **Critical Focus** as a prerequisite and are designed to amplify the impact of a critical hit, not increase the probability of landing one.

---

If you're looking for feats that **improve the chance of scoring a critical hit**, consider:

1. **Critical Focus** (Prerequisite for most critical feats):  
   - Grants a +1 bonus on attack rolls to confirm critical hits.  
   - *Source*: [Critical Focus](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/feats/combat-feats/critical-focus-combat).

2. **Improved Critical** (from *Advanced Player’s Guide*):  
   - Increases the threat range of a weapon by 1 (e.g., a threat range of 19–20 becomes 18–20).  
   - *Source*: [Improved Critical](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/feats/combat-feats/improved-critical-combat).

This ability is distinct from unarmed strike damage progression or style strikes, which add effects rather than extra attacks.

- **Smite Evil (Su)**: Once per day, a paladin can target an evil creature. They add their Charisma modifier to attack rolls and their paladin level to all damage rolls against the target.

  - **Duration**: The effect lasts until the target is dead, the paladin rests, or the ability is used again.

answer:
The **Ranger** class in Pathfinder 1e has two primary features that let it fight specific types of enemies better:

1. **Favored Enemy (Ex)** (Core Class Feature)  
   - At 1st level, the ranger selects a creature type (e.g., aberration, humanoid, undead) from the *Ranger Favored Enemies* table. They gain a **+2 bonus on attack and damage rolls against creatures of that type**. This bonus increases by +2 at 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th level.  
   - At 5th level, the ranger can select additional favored enemies, and the bonus for any one favored enemy can be stacked.  
   - **Source**: [Ranger Class Page](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/ranger).

2. **Ranger’s Focus (Ex)** (Guide Archetype)  
   - This archetype replaces *Favored Enemy* with **Ranger’s Focus**. At 1st level, the ranger can focus on a single enemy within line of sight as a swift action, gaining a **+2 bonus on attack and damage rolls against that target**. The bonus increases by +2 at 5th level and every five levels thereafter.  
   - The ability can be used additional times per day at 4th level and every three levels thereafter.  
   - **Source**: [Guide Archetype](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/ranger/archetypes/paizo-ranger-archetypes/guide).

Both features allow targeting specific enemies, but *Favored Enemy* is a core class trait, while *Ranger’s Focus* is an archetype replacement.

question: feat that lets you move through a threatened square safely
answer:
The feat **Weapon Trick (Warded Movement)** allows you to move through a threatened square safely. Here's how it works:

- **Prerequisites**: Dodge  
- **Benefit**: As a **swift action**, you can choose a foe you can see. You can **pass through that foe’s threatened area without provoking attacks of opportunity from that foe this round**. Once you target a foe with this trick, you can’t target it again that day.  

This feat specifically addresses moving through a threatened square without provoking attacks of opportunity, though it is limited to a single foe per day and requires a swift action.  

Another relevant feat is **Acrobatic Spellcaster (Combat)**, which allows moving through a threatened square safely when using Acrobatics, but it ties this benefit to spellcasting.  

For general movement through threatened squares, **Mobility** reduces the threat of attacks of opportunity but does not prevent provoking them.  

Source: [Weapon Trick (Warded Movement)](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/feats/combat-feats/weapon-trick-combat)

- **Effect**: The bard grants 2 bonus Hit Dice (d10s) to themselves or a single willing ally within 30 feet, along with a +2 competence bonus on attack rolls and a +1 competence bonus on Fortitude saves. The bonus Hit Dice count as regular Hit Dice for spells dependent on them. 
- **Scaling**: For every three levels beyond 9th, the bard can target one additional ally (up to four at 18th level).
- **Requirements**: All targets must see and hear the bard. The ability is mind-affecting and requires audible and visual components.

This feature is described on the [Bard class page](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/bard).

The skill used to balance, tumble, or avoid falling is **Acrobatics** (Dexterity-based, with an Armor Check Penalty). It covers:

- **Balance**: Keeping equilibrium on narrow or treacherous surfaces (DCs vary by surface width, e.g., 1–3 feet wide = DC 5).
- **Tumble**: Avoiding attacks of opportunity when moving through threatened squares (DC = opponent’s CMD; +5 if moving through an enemy’s space).
- **Softening Falls**: Deliberately falling and ignoring the first 10 feet of damage with a DC 15 Acrobatics check.

Additional modifiers apply for conditions like slippery surfaces, slopes, or unstable terrain (e.g., +5 for severely slippery, +10 for severely unsteady).  

Source: [Consolidated Skills Optional Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/skills/consolidated-skills-optional-rules).

question: what does Shoes of Lightning Leaping do
answer:
The **Shoes of Lightning Leaping** allow the wearer to once per day transform into lightning and move up to 50 feet in a straight line, re-materializing at the far end. Creatures in the path take **6d6 electricity damage**, and objects take damage as per the *lightning bolt* spell. If the lightning strikes an object or barrier and fails to pass through, the wearer appears next to it and is **staggered for 1 round**. Movement in lightning form does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

question: how do you avoid provoking an attack of opportunity when moving
answer:
To avoid provoking an attack of opportunity when moving, you can use either the **5-foot step** or the **withdraw action**. 

- A **5-foot step** is a free action that allows you to move up to 5 feet without provoking an attack of opportunity. This is useful for minor repositioning.  
- The **withdraw action** (a standard action) lets you move up to twice your speed, but you must move away from an opponent. This avoids provoking attacks of opportunity as long as you do not pass through a threatened square unnecessarily. 

Both methods are detailed in the [Combat section of the Pathfinder rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat).

question: how does flanking work and what bonus does it give
answer:
Flanking in Pathfinder 1e grants a **+2 bonus on attack rolls** against an opponent if the defender is threatened by another enemy on their opposite border or corner. To determine if two attackers flank an opponent:

1. Draw an imaginary line between the attackers' centers.
2. If the line passes through **opposite borders** (or corners of those borders) of the defender's space, flanking occurs.

**Key rules**:
- Only creatures that **threaten the defender** can contribute to flanking.
- Creatures with **0 reach** cannot flank.
- If a flanking creature occupies **multiple squares**, any square that contributes to flanking grants the bonus (e.g., a large creature covering multiple squares).

Example: If a fighter and cleric are adjacent to an ogre on opposite sides, they both gain a +2 bonus against it. A rogue not adjacent to the ogre or not threatening it cannot flank (see [Combat Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat)). 

Source: [https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat)

Flanking in Pathfinder 1e grants a **+2 bonus on attack rolls** against an opponent if the defender is threatened by another enemy on their opposite border or corner. To determine if two attackers flank an opponent:

1. Draw an imaginary line between the attackers' centers.
2. If the line passes through **opposite borders** (or corners of those borders) of the defender's space, flanking occurs.

**Key rules**:
- Only creatures that **threaten the defender** can contribute to flanking.
- Creatures with **0 reach** cannot flank.
- If a flanking creature occupies **multiple squares**, any square that contributes to flanking grants the bonus (e.g., a large creature covering multiple squares).

Example: If a fighter and cleric are adjacent to an ogre on opposite sides, they both gain a +2 bonus against it. A rogue not adjacent to the ogre or not threatening it cannot flank (see [Combat Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat)). 

Source: [https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat)

question: what happens if you're grappled and try to cast a spell

answer:
The formula for calculating **Combat Maneuver Defense (CMD)** is:

**CMD = 10 + Base Attack Bonus + Strength modifier + Dexterity modifier + special size modifier + miscellaneous modifiers**

This is explicitly stated in the *Combat* section of the Pathfinder rules (see [d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat)). 

- **Base Attack Bonus** is derived from your class levels and abilities.  
- **Strength modifier** is your Strength score adjusted for Even/Odd scores (e.g., +2 for 14, +3 for 15).  
- **Dexterity modifier** is your Dexterity score adjusted similarly.  
- **Special size modifier** depends on your size category (e.g., Medium +0, Large +1, Gargantuan +4).  
- **Miscellaneous modifiers** include feats (e.g., *Improved Combat Maneuver*), spells, or other effects that specifically alter CMD.  

For example, a Medium humanoid with a +6 Base Attack Bonus, +3 Strength, +2 Dexterity, and no other modifiers would have a CMD of **21** (10 + 6 + 3 + 2 = 21).

question: how does spell resistance interact with touch attacks
answer:
Spell resistance interacts with touch attacks as follows: When a spell with a touch attack is cast at a target that has spell resistance, the caster must make a caster level check (1d20 + caster level) against the target’s spell resistance. If the check succeeds, the spell affects the target; if it fails, the spell is negated. 

Spell resistance functions like an Armor Class against magical attacks. The target’s spell resistance value is compared to the caster’s check. Note that spell resistance only applies when the target is directly targeted by the spell (e.g., via a touch attack), not when encountering a spell already in effect. 

For harmless spells (e.g., *Resist Energy*, *Imbue with Spell Ability*), the target can voluntarily lower their resistance as a standard action to allow the spell to take effect without requiring a caster level check. 

Source: [Magic (d20pfsrd.com)](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/magic)

1. **Spell Resistance Mechanics**: Spell resistance (SR) acts like an Armor Class (AC) against magical attacks. 2. **Touch Attacks and AC**: Touch attacks (melee or ranged) ignore the target's armor bonus, shield bonus, and natural armor bonus. The target's AC for a touch attack includes only size modifier, Dexterity modifier, and deflection bonus (if any) (Combat > Touch Attacks, [URL](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat)).

3. **Interaction**:
   - If a spell is delivered via a touch attack, **spell resistance is checked when the spell is cast**, not during the touch attack roll. The caster must succeed on a caster level check to overcome the target's SR, regardless of whether the touch attack hits.
   - The **touch attack itself** is resolved separately, using the touch attack rules (e.g., no armor bonuses apply to the target's AC for the attack).
   - If the spell is resisted (caster level check fails), the spell has no effect, but the touch attack may still hit (if the attack roll succeeds) and deal damage (if applicable).

In summary, spell resistance applies to the spell's effect, while touch attacks resolve separately as an attack roll against the target's AC (excluding armor bonuses). They are distinct mechanics that both apply when a spell is cast as a touch attack.

question: can I move and attack in the same round
answer:
Yes, in Pathfinder 1e, you can move and attack in the same round under specific conditions:

1. **Standard Action + Move Action**: You can take a move action (moving up to your speed) and a standard action (such as attacking) in the same round. This is the most straightforward method.

2. **Charge**: If you charge, you must move **before** attacking. You move at least 10 feet (2 squares) directly toward the target, and may move up to double your speed. If you have a base attack bonus of +1 or higher, you can draw a weapon during the charge as part of the attack.

3. **Full Attack with Movement (Mobile Melee Variant)**: If using the *Mobile Melee* variant rule, you can declare movement during a melee full attack. You may move up to your speed, but for every 5 feet moved beyond the first 5 feet, you take a –5 penalty on attack rolls (reduced to –4 with the *Spring Attack* feat). This allows moving **during** a full attack, not just before or after.

4. **Withdraw or 5-Foot Step**: You can take a 5-foot step (no movement provokes attacks of opportunity) before, during, or after other actions. However, you cannot take a 5-foot step if you move any distance in the same round.

**Penalties and Restrictions**:
- Moving during a full attack (via *Mobile Melee*) incurs penalties unless you have *Spring Attack*.
- Charging requires a clear path and cannot be combined with a 5-foot step.
- If you take a full-round action (e.g., *Full Attack*), you can only take a 5-foot step, not move otherwise.

Yes, in Pathfinder 1e, you can move and attack in the same round under specific conditions:

1. **Standard Action + Move Action**: You can take a move action (moving up to your speed) and a standard action (such as attacking) in the same round. This is the most straightforward method.

2. **Charge**: If you charge, you must move **before** attacking. You move at least 10 feet (2 squares) directly toward the target, and may move up to double your speed. If you have a base attack bonus of +1 or higher, you can draw a weapon during the charge as part of the attack.

3. **Full Attack with Movement (Mobile Melee Variant)**: If using the *Mobile Melee* variant rule, you can declare movement during a melee full attack. You may move up to your speed, but for every 5 feet moved beyond the first 5 feet, you take a –5 penalty on attack rolls (reduced to –4 with the *Spring Attack* feat). This allows moving **during** a full attack, not just before or after.

4. **Withdraw or 5-Foot Step**: You can take a 5-foot step (no movement provokes attacks of opportunity) before, during, or after other actions. However, you cannot take a 5-foot step if you move any distance in the same round.

**Penalties and Restrictions**:
- Moving during a full attack (via *Mobile Melee*) incurs penalties unless you have *Spring Attack*.
- Charging requires a clear path and cannot be combined with a 5-foot step.
- If you take a full-round action (e.g., *Full Attack*), you can only take a 5-foot step, not move otherwise.

- Charging requires a clear path and cannot be combined with a 5-foot step.

- You cannot take a 5-foot step and move any distance in the same round.

In Pathfinder 1e, you can move and attack in the same round under specific conditions:

1. **Charging**:  
   You can move **up to double your speed** directly toward a target and then attack. You must move at least 10 feet (2 squares) before attacking. If you have a base attack bonus of +1 or higher, you can also draw a weapon during the charge (see [Combat > Charge](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat#TOC-Charge)).

2. **Full Attack with Movement (Mobile Melee Variant)**:  
   When declaring a melee full attack, you can move up to your speed **before or after attacks**. For every 5 feet moved beyond the first 5 feet, you take a –5 penalty on attack rolls (see [Removing Iterative Attacks > Mobile Melee](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/unchained-rules/removing-iterative-attacks)).

3. **Combining Actions**:  
   If you take a **move action** and a **standard action** in the same round, you can move your speed and perform an attack (e.g., attacking with a weapon or casting a spell). If you move out of a threatened square, you provoke an attack of opportunity unless you take a 5-foot step (see [Combat > Movement](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat#TOC-Movement)).

**Key Restrictions**:  
- Charging requires a clear path and cannot be combined with a 5-foot step.  
- Moving during a full attack incurs penalties unless you have the *Spring Attack* feat (–4 instead of –5 per 5 feet moved).  
- You cannot take a 5-foot step and move any distance in the same round.

**Conclusion**: Concealment and cover are separate modifiers. Concealment affects miss chance (but does not stack with itself), while cover affects AC. They do not combine to increase miss chance further.

question: can you cast a spell while threatened without provoking an attack

question: how does a rogue qualify to deal sneak attack damage
answer:
A rogue qualifies to deal sneak attack damage under the following conditions, as detailed on the [Rogue class page](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/rogue):

1. **Denied Dexterity Bonus**: The target is denied a Dexterity bonus to AC (e.g., due to being flat-footed, stunned, or otherwise unable to use Dexterity for defense).
2. **Flanking**: The rogue flanks the target (with an ally adjacent to the target on the opposite side).
3. **Weapon Type**: The attack uses a weapon that deals nonlethal damage (e.g., sap, whip, unarmed strike) if the rogue wishes to deal nonlethal sneak attack damage. Lethal weapons cannot be used for nonlethal sneak attacks, even with penalties.
4. **Line of Sight**: The rogue must see the target well enough to target a vital spot.
5. **No Concealment**: The target cannot have total concealment (e.g., being invisible or behind total cover).

**Damage Progression**:  
Sneak attack damage starts at 1d6 at 1st level and increases by 1d6 every two rogue levels (e.g., 2d6 at 3rd level, 3d6 at 5th level, etc.). This damage is precision damage and is **not multiplied** on a critical hit. Ranged sneak attacks are only valid if the target is within 30 feet.

The damage starts at **1d6** at 1st level and increases by **1d6 every two rogue levels**. This damage is precision damage and is not multiplied on a critical hit.

question: how do multiple attacks of opportunity in one round work with combat reflexes
answer:
Combat Reflexes allows a character to make additional attacks of opportunity equal to their Dexterity modifier (minimum 1) per round. However, the total number of attacks of opportunity is limited by the character's base number of attacks per round. For example, a character with a Dexterity modifier of +3 can make 1 (base) + 3 = **4 attacks of opportunity** per round, but only if their base attack count permits that many attacks.

Key interactions:
- **Stacking Abilities**: Some abilities (like Kensai's *Superior Reflexes*) can add to the number of attacks of opportunity, stacking with Combat Reflexes (e.g., adding Intelligence modifier).
- **Limitations**: Certain abilities (e.g., *Opportunist*) may restrict their use to once per round, even with Combat Reflexes.
- **Cap**: You cannot make more attacks of opportunity than your total number of attacks per round. For example, if your base attack count is 2, you cannot exceed 2 attacks of opportunity, even if Combat Reflexes would allow more.

Source: [Opportunist (Ex)](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/rogue/rogue-talents/paizo-rogue-advanced-talents/opportunist-ex) and [Kensai](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/base-classes/magus/archetypes/paizo-magus-archetypes/kensai).

When using Combat Reflexes with multiple attacks of opportunity in a single round, here's how it works:

1. **Base Mechanics**: Normally, a character can make **1 attack of opportunity per round** (per opponent), and cannot make attacks of opportunity while flat-footed.

2. **Combat Reflexes Bonus**: With the **Combat Reflexes** feat, you can make **additional attacks of opportunity** equal to your **Dexterity bonus** (including any modifiers). For example, if your Dexterity bonus is +4, you can make **5 attacks of opportunity** total (1 normal +4 from the feat).

3. **Triggering Multiple Attacks**:
   - Each attack of opportunity must be **triggered by a separate provocation** (e.g., an opponent moving through a threatened square, performing an action that provokes, etc.).
   - If the **same opponent provokes multiple opportunities** in the same round (e.g., by moving through multiple threatened squares), you can make **multiple attacks of opportunity** against them, as each provocation is a separate opportunity.
   - However, **moving out of multiple squares threatened by the same opponent** in the same round does **not** count as multiple opportunities—only one attack of opportunity is allowed per opponent per round, even if they provoke multiple times.

4. **Attack Bonuses**: All attacks of opportunity are made at your **full normal attack bonus**, regardless of how many you make in a round.

5. **Limitations**:
   - You cannot make more than **one attack of opportunity per provocation** (even with Combat Reflexes).
   - The feat does **not** allow you to make attacks of opportunity for the same provocation multiple times.

**Source**: [Combat Reflexes Feat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/feats/combat-feats/combat-reflexes-combat) and [Attacks of Opportunity Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat).

question: does a critical hit multiply extra damage dice like sneak attack
answer:
According to the Pathfinder 1e rules on critical hits:

**Extra damage dice (such as from sneak attack) are not multiplied** on a critical hit. The rule explicitly states:  
> "*Exception*: Precision damage (such as from a rogue’s sneak attack class feature) and additional damage dice from special weapon qualities (such as flaming) are not multiplied when you score a critical hit."  

Critical hits only multiply the base weapon damage (e.g., a ×2 or ×3 multiplier applied to the weapon's normal damage dice). Sneak attack dice and similar effects are added **after** the critical hit multiplier is applied, and they are not multiplied further.  

Source: [https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat)

According to the Pathfinder 1e rules on critical hits:

**Extra damage dice (such as from sneak attack) are not multiplied** on a critical hit. The rule explicitly states:  
> "*Exception*: Precision damage (such as from a rogue’s sneak attack class feature) and additional damage dice from special weapon qualities (such as flaming) are not multiplied when you score a critical hit."  

Critical hits only multiply the base weapon damage (e.g., a ×2 or ×3 multiplier applied to the weapon's normal damage dice). Sneak attack dice and similar effects are added **after** the critical hit multiplier is applied, and they are not multiplied further.  

Source: [https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat)

question: how does a barbarian's fatigue after rage interact with fatigued condition already in effect
answer:
The fatigue from a barbarian's rage interacts with existing fatigue as follows:

1. **Rage-Induced Fatigue**: When a barbarian ends her rage, she becomes fatigued for a number of rounds equal to **2 × the number of rounds spent in rage** (Core Barbarian, [source](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/barbarian)). 

2. **Interaction with Existing Fatigue**: The rules do not explicitly address stacking with pre-existing fatigue. However, since the fatigue from rage is a **specific duration** (calculated based on rage rounds), it replaces any existing fatigue condition that would otherwise be active at the same time. question: how does spell failure chance work when casting in armor
answer:
When casting spells while wearing armor in Pathfinder 1e, **arcane spell failure chance** depends on the type of armor, the presence of a shield, and whether the spell has a **somatic component**. Here's how it works:

1. **Spells Without Somatic Components**  
   - Can be cast **without arcane spell failure chance** in any armor or while bound/grappling (concentration checks still apply).  
   - Example: Using the *Still Spell* metamagic feat to remove the somatic component.

2. **Spells With Somatic Components**  
   - **Armor and shields** impose an arcane spell failure chance, listed in their descriptions.  
   - Example: A *breastplate* might have a 20% failure chance, while *chainmail* might have 30% (exact values vary by item).

3. **Class-Specific Exceptions**  
   - **Summoners**: Can cast summoner spells in **light armor** without failure. Medium/heavy armor or shields still apply normal rules.  
   - **Bards**: Can cast in **light armor** and use shields without failure. Medium/heavy armor applies normal rules.  
   - **Magus**: Gains proficiency with **light armor** (no failure chance for magus spells) at 1st level, **medium armor** at 7th, and **heavy armor** at 13th.  
   - **Child of War** (fighter archetype): Reduces arcane spell failure chance by 15–30% (depending on level) as a swift action.

4. **General Rule**  
   - If a spell has a somatic component, the caster must **succeed on a check** (DC 10 + spell’s level + armor/shield’s failure chance) to cast it while wearing armor. Failure means the spell is lost.

For exact percentages, check the **armor** or **shield** description (e.g., [Chainmail](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/equipment/armor/medium-armor/chainmail/), [Tower Shield](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/equipment/shields/tower-shield/)). 

Source: [Arcanist](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/hybrid-classes/arcanist), [Wizard](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/wizard), [Summoner](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/base-classes/summoner), [Bard](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/bard), [Magus](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/base-classes/magus).

4. **Bards**: Bards can wear light armor (e.g., *rosewood armor*) and use shields without incurring arcane spell failure chance for their bard spells.

question: what is the difference between a fortitude, reflex, and will save in practice
answer:
In Pathfinder, the three types of saving throws—**Fortitude**, **Reflex**, and **Will**—differ in their purposes and the ability scores they rely on:

1. **Fortitude**  
   - **Purpose**: Resists effects that target the body, such as **poisons, diseases, and non-magical physical trauma** (e.g., *giant slime*’s engulf ability).  
   - **Linked Ability Score**: **Constitution**.  
   - Example: A character with a high Constitution modifier gains a +4 bonus to Fortitude saves against diseases.  

2. **Reflex**  
   - **Purpose**: Avoids **area attacks** or threats that can be dodged, such as *fireball*, *acid splash*, or falling damage.  
   - **Linked Ability Score**: **Dexterity**.  
   - Example: A rogue with high Dexterity might avoid a *fireball*’s blast radius entirely via a Reflex save.  

3. **Will**  
   - **Purpose**: Resists **mental effects** like *charm person*, *mind fog*, or *magic missile* (if the spell has a Will save).  
   - **Linked Ability Score**: **Wisdom**.  
   - Example: A wizard with high Wisdom might negate a *charm monster* spell’s effect via a Will save.  

All saving throws are **automatic** and do not require an action. They are determined by the relevant ability score modifier plus any applicable bonuses (e.g., from magic items or spells).  

Source: [https://www.d20pfsrd.com/basics-ability-scores/glossary](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/basics-ability-scores/glossary)

3. **Will**  
   - **Purpose**: Resists **mental and magical effects** (e.g., *charm person*, *mind fog*, or illusions).  
   - **Ability Score**: **Wisdom (Wis)**.

   - **Related Mechanics**: Wisdom bonuses also enhance Will saves and spell DCs (see [Ability Scores](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/basics-ability-scores/ability-scores)).

In Pathfinder, the three types of saving throws—**Fortitude**, **Reflex**, and **Will**—serve distinct purposes and are influenced by different ability scores:

1. **Fortitude**  
   - **Purpose**: Resists **bodily ailments** (e.g., poison, disease, fatigue, or effects that damage health).  
   - **Ability Score**: **Constitution (Con)**.  
   - Example: Resisting the effects of a *plague* spell or avoiding illness.  
   - **Related Mechanics**: Temporary increases to Constitution boost Fortitude saves and add hit points (see [Ability Scores](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/basics-ability-scores/ability-scores)).

2. **Reflex**  
   - **Purpose**: Avoids **area-of-effect threats** (e.g., *fireball*, *cone of cold*, or falling damage).  
   - **Ability Score**: **Dexterity (Dex)**.  
   - Example: Dodging a *fireball* explosion or avoiding trap damage.  
   - **Related Mechanics**: Dexterity bonuses also improve Armor Class (AC) and initiative (see [Ability Scores](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/basics-ability-scores/ability-scores)).

3. **Will**  
   - **Purpose**: Resists **mental and magical effects** (e.g., *charm person*, *mind fog*, or illusions).  
   - **Ability Score**: **Wisdom (Wis)**.  
   - Example: Resisting a *phantom fortress* illusion or a *geas* spell.  
   - **Related Mechanics**: Wisdom bonuses also enhance Will saves and spell DCs (see [Ability Scores](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/basics-ability-scores/ability-scores)).

**Key Difference**:  
Fortitude is about **surviving physical harm**, Reflex is about **avoiding threats**, and Will is about **resisting mental or magical influence**. Each is tied to a core ability score that defines a character’s resilience in those areas.  

Source: [Common Terms > Saving Throw](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/basics-ability-scores/glossary)

The differences between Fortitude, Reflex, and Will saving throws in Pathfinder are defined by their purpose and the ability modifiers they use:

1. **Fortitude**  
   - **Purpose**: Measures resistance to **physical damage or attacks against vitality/health** (e.g., poison, disease, non-lethal damage, or effects that bypass armor).  
   - **Modifier**: **Constitution**.  
   - *Example*: Saving against a *slow* spell that targets your body or a *cloudkill* cloud’s toxic damage.  

2. **Reflex**  
   - **Purpose**: Tests the ability to **dodge area attacks or unexpected dangers** (e.g., explosions, traps, or environmental hazards).  
   - **Modifier**: **Dexterity**.  
   - *Example*: Avoiding damage from a *fireball* spell or a *web* trap.  

3. **Will**  
   - **Purpose**: Reflects resistance to **mental influence or magical effects that target the mind** (e.g., fear, charm, mind control, or illusion).  
   - **Modifier**: **Wisdom**.  
   - *Example*: Resisting a *charm person* spell or a *geas* compulsion.  

These distinctions are outlined in the [Pathfinder Combat rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat). Each save type is used in different scenarios, and their associated ability modifiers ensure characters are vulnerable to threats that align with their weaknesses.

The differences between Fortitude, Reflex, and Will saving throws in Pathfinder are defined by their purpose and the ability modifiers they use:

1. **Fortitude**  
   - **Purpose**: Measures resistance to **physical damage or attacks against vitality/health** (e.g., poison, disease, non-lethal damage, or effects that bypass armor).  
   - **Modifier**: **Constitution**.  
   - *Example*: Saving against a *slow* spell that targets your body or a *cloudkill* cloud’s toxic damage.  

2. **Reflex**  
   - **Purpose**: Tests the ability to **dodge area attacks or unexpected dangers** (e.g., explosions, traps, or environmental hazards).  
   - **Modifier**: **Dexterity**.  
   - *Example*: Avoiding damage from a *fireball* spell or a *web* trap.  

3. **Will**  
   - **Purpose**: Reflects resistance to **mental influence or magical effects that target the mind** (e.g., fear, charm, mind control, or illusion).  
   - **Modifier**: **Wisdom**.  
   - *Example*: Resisting a *charm person* spell or a *geas* compulsion.  

These distinctions are outlined in the [Pathfinder Combat rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat). Each save type is used in different scenarios, and their associated ability modifiers ensure characters are vulnerable to threats that align with their weaknesses.

question: how does channel energy affect undead versus living creatures
answer:
Channel Energy typically affects undead and living creatures based on the type of energy channeled (positive or negative). Here's a breakdown:

### Standard Effect (Cleric Class):
- **Positive Energy**: Heals living creatures, damages undead. Living targets take damage and can attempt a **Will save** to halve it. Undead take damage and also get a **Will save** to halve it. Healing does not exceed the target's maximum HP.
- **Negative Energy**: Damages living creatures, heals undead. Living targets take damage with a **Will save** to halve it. Undead are healed (no save).

**Source**: [Cleric Class Features](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/cleric).

---

### Exceptions/Variations:
1. **Elder Mythos Cultist (Archetype)**:
   - **Channel the Void**: Deals non-energy damage (supernatural deterioration) to **living beings, corporeal non-skeletal undead, and flesh constructs**. Targets get a **Fortitude save** instead of Will. At 8th level, failed saves result in disintegration.
   - **Source**: [Elder Mythos Cultist](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/core-classes/cleric/archetypes/paizo-cleric-archetypes/elder-mythos-cultist-cleric-archetype).

2. **Death Slayer (Prestige Class)**:
   - **Channel Energy**: Only damages undead (no healing). Uses **Will saves** (DC: 10 + class level + Charisma modifier).
   - **Source**: [Death Slayer](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/prestige-classes/other-paizo/c-d/death-slayer).

3. **Warpriest (Class)**:
   - **Alignment-Based**: Good warpriests use **positive energy** (heal living, damage undead). Evil ones use **negative energy** (damage living, heal undead). Neutral warpriests depend on spell choices.
   - **Source**: [Warpriest](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/hybrid-classes/warpriest).

4. **Hex Channeler (Archetype)**:
   - Functions like a cleric, with **positive/negative energy** affecting living/undead as standard. No holy symbol required.
   - **Source**: [Hex Channeler](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/classes/base-classes/witch/archetypes/paizo-witch-archetypes/hex-channeler).

---

### Special Cases:
- **Necromancy (Wizard School)**: Allows Command Undead/Turn Undead via Channel Energy, targeting undead only.
- **Ranger Traps**: Can use channeled energy (positive/negative) to harm either undead or living, with a **Will save**.
- **Variant Channeling**: Describes thematic effects (e.g., "pale grey light," "spirit manifestations") but follows standard energy-type rules.

Always check the specific class or archetype for nuances, as effects may vary.

1. **Vital Strike Requirement**: Vital Strike (and its improved/greater variants) requires using an **attack action**, a type of standard action where you make one attack (with extra damage dice rolls).

   > "No. Vital Strike can only be used as part of an attack action [...] Charging is a special kind of full-round action that includes the ability to make one melee attack, not one attack action."

   - The **Divine Fighting Technique** feat (linked to specific gods) allows using Vital Strike with a greatsword **at the end of a charge**, but this is a rare, feat-dependent exception.  
   - Other feats (e.g., *Gravitational Vital Strike*) may modify Vital Strike in specific contexts, but none generalize to all charge attacks.

**Conclusion**: Without a specific feat granting an exception, Vital Strike and charge attacks are incompatible due to differing action types.

question: how do size categories affect combat maneuver checks
answer:
Size categories in Pathfinder 1e affect **Combat Maneuver Bonus (CMB)** and **Combat Maneuver Defense (CMD)** through specific modifiers, as detailed in the *Combat* section of the rules:

### **Combat Maneuver Bonus (CMB)**
- Creatures **Tiny or smaller** use their **Dexterity modifier** instead of their **Strength modifier** when calculating CMB.
- **Special size modifiers** for CMB are applied as follows:
  - Fine: –8  
  - Diminutive: –4  
  - Tiny: –2  
  - Small: –1  
  - Medium: +0  
  - Large: +1  
  - Huge: +2  
  - Gargantuan: +4  
  - Colossal: +8  

### **Combat Maneuver Defense (CMD)**
- The **special size modifier** for CMD is identical to the CMB modifiers listed above. For example, a **Small** creature gains a –1 modifier to its CMD.

### Additional Notes
- The **"Special Size Modifier"** section explicitly states these values apply to both CMB and CMD (see [Combat > Special Attacks > Combat Maneuvers](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat)).
- Some exceptions exist (e.g., certain feats or abilities may alter these modifiers), but the base rules are as described.

question: what happens to your caster level if you're at negative hit points
answer:
In Pathfinder 1e, being at negative hit points does not directly impose a **caster level penalty** under standard rules. However, specific optional rules or conditions may alter this:

1. **Wound Thresholds (Optional Rule)**: If your GM uses the *Wound Thresholds* optional rules, being wounded or critical (which can occur when at negative hit points) imposes a **penalty to caster level**. This reduces the effectiveness of spells (range, duration, etc.) and concentration checks, but the caster level can’t drop below 1. This is detailed in the [Wound Thresholds Optional Rules](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/unchained-rules/wound-thresholds-optional-rules).

2. **Negative Levels**: If negative levels are applied (e.g., via spells like *energy drain*), they reduce your effective level for **level-dependent variables**, including spellcasting. Each negative level makes you treat yourself as one level lower. This is covered in the [Special Abilities](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/special-abilities) page.

3. **Standard Rules**: Under normal Pathfinder rules, simply being at negative hit points (dying) does not reduce caster level. Spellcasters retain their spellcasting ability even when at negative hit points, as noted in the [Combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat) rules.

**Conclusion**: Unless specific optional rules (like *Wound Thresholds*) or effects (like *negative levels*) are in play, **caster level is not reduced** by being at negative hit points.

When a spellcaster is at negative hit points, the impact on their caster level depends on the rules in effect:

1. **Core Rules**: Being at negative hit points does not directly reduce a spellcaster's caster level. Spellcasting capabilities are only lost if the character dies (per [Combat > Injury and Death](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/combat#TOC-Injury-and-Death)), but prepared spells and spell slots are not lost from negative hit points alone.

2. **Wound Thresholds (Optional Rule)**: Under the optional *Wound Thresholds* rules, if a character is in the "wounded" or "critical" condition (which applies when hit points drop below thresholds tied to Constitution), they suffer a **penalty to caster level**. This reduces the effectiveness of spells (range, duration, etc.) and concentration checks, but the penalty cannot reduce caster level below 1. This is detailed in [Wound Thresholds Optional Rules > Caster Level Penalties](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/unchained-rules/wound-thresholds-optional-rules#TOC-Caster-Level-Penalties).

3. **Negative Levels**: If the character has negative levels (from effects like *energy drain*), each negative level reduces their effective level for level-dependent variables (including caster level) by 1, but this is separate from negative hit points. See [Special Abilities > Energy Drain and Negative Levels](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/special-abilities#TOC-Energy-Drain-and-Negative-Levels).

**Summary**: In the core rules, negative hit points do not penalize caster level. However, if your GM uses the *Wound Thresholds* optional rules, being wounded or critical may impose a caster level penalty. Negative levels (from spells/undead) also reduce effective caster level, but this is distinct from negative hit points.

To kill a lich, you must destroy its **phylactery**, the magical vessel containing its soul. Simply destroying its physical body is insufficient, as the phylactery will regenerate the lich’s form over 1d10 days if not destroyed. The phylactery is typically hidden in a secure location, and the lich may guard it fiercely.

### Key Mechanics:
- **Phylactery Destruction**: Destroying the phylactery is the only way to permanently kill a lich. This requires a **DC 30 spellcraft check** to locate it, as it is often hidden using *mending* or other concealment magic.
- **Damage Types**: A lich has **DR 15/bludgeoning and magic**, immune to **cold and electricity**, and **channel resistance +4**. Attacks dealing **positive energy** (e.g., *Smite Undead*) or **piercing/bludgeoning** damage (e.g., *Disintegrate*, *Massmorph*, or *Shatter* spells) are most effective.
- **Special Abilities**: 
  - **Paralyzing Touch (Su)**: Can paralyze living creatures, but does not affect the lich itself.
  - **Rejuvenation (Su)**: If the lich’s body is destroyed, its phylactery rebuilds it after 1d10 days.

### Strategic Considerations:
- **Target the Phylactery**: Use spells like *Find Traps* (to detect magical items) or *Divination* to locate it. Once found, destroy it with a *Disintegrate* spell, *Wish*, or a *Rod of Resurrection*.
- **Bypass DR**: Use **piercing** or **bludgeoning** attacks, and consider effects that ignore DR (e.g., *Mending* to bypass DR from *Force* effects).
- **Avoid Immunities**: Avoid cold, electricity, or illusion-based attacks, as they are ineffective.

answer:
When traversing wilderness, the primary check required to avoid getting lost is a **Survival check**, as outlined in the [Wilderness](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/environment/wilderness) rules:

- **DCs vary by terrain** (e.g., **Desert/Plains**: 14, **Forest**: 16, **Mountain**: 12, **Open Sea**: 18).

For marshes or rugged terrain, additional Survival DC increases apply (see [Exploration & Movement in Sandbox Campaigns](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/exploration-and-movement-sandbox)).

question: How would I assess if a ship is likely to sink
answer:
To assess if a ship is likely to sink in Pathfinder 1e, refer to the rules on ship combat and conditions:

1. **Hit Points and Sinking Condition**:  
   A ship gains the **sinking condition** if its hit points (HP) are reduced to **0 or fewer**. Once this happens, the ship cannot move or attack and will **sink completely 10 rounds later** (source: [Ship Combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/ship-combat)).

2. **Damage Reduction During Sinking**:  
   Each hit on a sinking ship that inflicts **25 points of damage** reduces the remaining time to sink by **1 round** (source: [Ultimate Ships](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/ultimate-ships)).

3. **Repairing a Ship**:  
   - **Magic**: Spells like *Make Whole* can raise a sinking ship’s HP above 0, removing the sinking condition.  
   - **Non-magical Repairs**: These are too slow to prevent sinking once the condition is active (source: [Conditions](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/conditions)).

4. **Broken Condition (Pre-sinking)**:  
   A ship gains the **broken condition** when its HP drops to **half or below**. This imposes penalties (e.g., –2 to AC, sailing checks, and speed is halved) but does not immediately cause sinking (source: [Advanced Naval Combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/ship-combat/advanced-naval-combat)).

**Summary**: Monitor the ship’s HP. If it reaches 0, it will sink in 10 rounds unless repaired via magic. Damage dealt while sinking accelerates this process.

   A ship gains the **sinking condition** if its hit points (HP) are reduced to **0 or fewer**. Once this happens, the ship cannot move or attack and will **sink completely 10 rounds later** (source: [Ship Combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/ship-combat)).

2. **Damage Reduction During Sinking**:  
   Each hit on a sinking ship that inflicts **25 points of damage** reduces the remaining time to sink by **1 round** (source: [Ultimate Ships](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/ultimate-ships)).

   - **Magic**: Spells like *Make Whole* can raise a sinking ship’s HP above 0, removing the sinking condition.

   A ship gains the **broken condition** when its HP drops to **half or below**. 1. **Sinking Condition Triggers**:
   - A ship gains the **sinking condition** when its **hit points (HP) are reduced to 0 or fewer** (see [Conditions](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/conditions), [Ship Combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/ship-combat), and [Advanced Naval Combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/ship-combat/advanced-naval-combat)).

2. **Time to Sink**:
   - A sinking ship has **10 rounds** to sink completely. Each **hit dealing over 25 damage** reduces this time by 1 round (see [Conditions](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/conditions), [Ship Combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/ship-combat)).

3. **Repairing a Sinking Ship**:
   - **Magic** (e.g., *Make Whole*) can raise HP above 0, removing the sinking condition. **Non-magical repairs** are too slow to save a ship once it begins sinking ([Conditions](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/conditions), [Advanced Naval Combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/ship-combat/advanced-naval-combat)).

4. **Broken Condition**:
   - Ships take a **–2 penalty** to AC, sailing checks, and saving throws when they reach **half their HP** (see [Advanced Naval Combat](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/ship-combat/advanced-naval-combat)).

**Destroyed Ships**: A ship that sinks completely is **destroyed** and cannot be repaired ([Conditions](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/conditions), [Vehicles](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/other-rules/vehicles)).

If you’re **pinned** instead of merely grappled, you also cannot cast spells with somatic or material components (see [Pinned condition](https://www.d20pfsrd.com/gamemastering/conditions)).
